Project Milestones: MVP Release Vision, MMP Release Vision
Deliverable Description: A vision board is a simple, visual snapshot of where a product is headed and the future it is trying to create. Teams use it to capture the big idea in a form everyone can see and rally around before diving into the details.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It gives the team a shared thing to aim at, so day-to-day choices line up with the larger goal instead of drifting apart.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It takes shape during the Vision milestone and sets the direction that later work like the roadmap, epics, and scope grows out of. Teams often revisit it as they learn more.

Workshops.label: Scenario-Based Problem Statement Generation Workshop Template

Deliverable Description: A problem statement is a short, clear description of the problem a team is solving, written from the user's point of view. It keeps everyone focused on the real issue instead of jumping straight to a solution.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: Teams that skip this often build something polished that solves the wrong problem. A sharp problem statement keeps the effort aimed at something that genuinely matters.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It emerges in Discovery and Requirements and feeds almost everything after it, from how-might-we statements to user stories and scope, and it gets sharper as the team learns.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

Workshops.label: Scenario-Based Problem Statement Generation Workshop Template

Deliverable Description: A problem checklist is a running list of the specific problems and needs a team has spotted and wants to address. It turns a vague sense that things are broken into concrete items the team can track.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It keeps real user problems from getting lost as the work speeds up, so the team can prioritize honestly instead of chasing whatever is loudest.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It grows in Discovery and Requirements alongside problem statements and helps shape what makes it into scope. The list keeps changing as new problems surface.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

Project Milestones: MVP Design Requirements, MVP Release Scope, MMP Release Scope, MMP Design Requirements, MMP Development Requirements, MVP Development Requirements
Deliverable Description: Epics and features are the mid-sized chunks a big idea gets broken into. An epic is a large body of work, and features are the smaller, usable pieces inside it that a team can actually build and ship.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: Breaking work this way lets an agile team deliver value in pieces instead of waiting to finish one giant thing, and it makes progress easy to see.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: They come out of the Requirements and Scope milestones and sit between the high-level roadmap and the detailed user stories the team builds from.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Project Milestones: MVP Release Scope, MMP Release Scope
Deliverable Description: Release-level scope is the decision about what will and will not be included in a particular release. It draws a clear line around a chunk of work so the team knows what they are committing to next.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: Without it, a release can balloon and never ship. Defining scope keeps a release focused and sets honest expectations with everyone involved.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It is set during the Scope milestone, sits below the roadmap, and shapes the epics, features, and backlog the team pulls from. Teams re-scope as priorities shift.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Project Milestones: MVP Design Requirements, MMP Design Requirements, MMP Development Requirements, MVP Development Requirements
Deliverable Description: Acceptance criteria are the plain, agreed conditions that tell everyone when a piece of work is truly done. They spell out what has to be true for a feature or story to be accepted.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: They stop the endless debate about whether something is finished, so designers, developers, and clients all share the same finish line.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: They attach to user stories in the Requirements milestone and guide the QA test plans and acceptance testing that check the work later on.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

Why Is This Deliverable Important?: Stories turn big requirements into small, buildable pieces the team can pick up one at a time, which is the heartbeat of agile delivery.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: They come from the Requirements milestone, carry acceptance criteria, and fill the backlog the team works through sprint by sprint.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

Deliverable Description: BDD scenarios describe how a feature should behave in plain, structured language, usually as given-when-then steps. They turn a requirement into a concrete example of what should happen.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: They give developers and testers one shared, unambiguous description to build and check against, which cuts down on misread requirements.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: They grow out of requirements and acceptance criteria and feed directly into QA test cases and acceptance testing near launch.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It builds on requirements and acceptance criteria, spins off into detailed test cases, and drives the acceptance testing milestone.
Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

Project Milestones: MMP Development Requirements, MVP Development Requirements

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It is created in Requirements, guides the more detailed architecture specs and diagrams, and shapes how developers build in the Implement milestone.
Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

Project Milestones: MVP Design Requirements
Deliverable Description: A task flow maps the steps a user takes to complete a single task, from start to finish. It shows the path through a product one goal at a time.

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Task flows come together in Requirements, lean on user stories and acceptance criteria, and guide the wireframes and prototypes designers create.

Project Milestones: MVP Design Requirements, Quality Assurance
Deliverable Description: A use case scenario walks through how someone uses a product to reach a goal, including the twists and turns along the way. It tells the story of the product in action.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It helps the team think through real situations, including the ones that are easy to forget, so fewer surprises show up during building.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Written in Requirements, use case scenarios build on user stories and inform use case diagrams, task flows, and acceptance criteria.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

Project Milestones: MVP Design Requirements
Deliverable Description: A use case diagram is a simple picture showing who uses a product and the main things they can do with it. It gives a quick, big-picture view of the product's functions.

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It comes from the Requirements milestone and summarizes the use case scenarios and user stories into one clear overview.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Created in Discovery, it informs the business plan, go-to-market plan, and positioning work, and it pairs with the competitive analysis.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Project Milestones: MVP Design, MMP Design, MMP Development Requirements, MVP Development Requirements
Deliverable Description: An editorial style guide is the rulebook for how a product's words sound, covering tone, wording, and formatting. It keeps the writing consistent no matter who is writing it.

Project Milestones: MVP Design, MMP Design
Deliverable Description: Brand identity is the personality of a product made visible and audible: its look, voice, and feel. It is what makes a product recognizable and distinct.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: A strong, consistent identity builds trust and makes a product memorable, tying the whole experience together.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It comes together in Implement and shapes the logo and brand assets, editorial style guide, and archetypes that flow from it.
Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

Deliverable Description: A user journey map traces a person's whole experience with a product over time, including what they do, think, and feel at each step. It shows the experience as a story, not a single screen.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It reveals the high and low points of an experience, so the team knows where to focus to make things better.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Built during Discovery from research, it connects to personas and empathy maps and guides design decisions across many milestones.
Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

Project Milestones: MVP Design
Deliverable Description: A user persona is a short, realistic profile of a typical user, based on research: their goals, needs, and frustrations. It puts a human face on the audience.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: Personas keep the team designing for real people instead of a vague 'user,' which leads to choices that actually fit someone's life.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Made in Discovery from research, they pair with journey maps and empathy maps and steer design and product decisions throughout the project.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Deliverable Description: A proto persona is a quick, best-guess profile of a user made before deep research, based on what the team already believes. It is a starting point, not a final answer.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It gives a team something concrete to align around early, as long as everyone remembers it is a hypothesis to test.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Created early in Discovery, proto personas are the rough draft that real research later turns into full user personas.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It helps the team and business speak to the people who actually pay, shaping pricing, messaging, and sales.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Built in Discovery, it complements user personas and feeds the marketing plan, positioning, and go-to-market work.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Project Milestones: MMP Release Vision, MMP Launch
Deliverable Description: A business plan lays out how a product will create and sustain value: the market, the model, the costs, and the goals. It is the big-picture case for why the product should exist.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It forces a team to think past the idea to whether it can actually work and last, which protects everyone from building something unsustainable.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Shaped in Discovery, it draws on market research and strategy and sets the frame for the marketing, release, and go-to-market plans.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Project Milestones: MMP Release Vision, MMP Launch
Deliverable Description: A marketing plan describes how a product will reach and win over its audience. It maps the channels, messages, and timing for getting the word out.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: Even a great product needs people to find it. A clear plan makes sure the work actually reaches the audience it was built for.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It runs across the whole project, builds on positioning and personas, and works hand in hand with the go-to-market and release plans.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Deliverable Description: A release plan lays out what will ship, when, and in what order across upcoming releases. It turns a roadmap into a concrete schedule of value going out the door.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It keeps the team and stakeholders aligned on what is coming next, and it supports shipping in steady pieces rather than one risky drop.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It connects the roadmap and scope to the go-to-market plan, and in agile work it is expected to shift as the team learns.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Project Milestones: MMP Release Vision, MMP Launch
Deliverable Description: A go-to-market plan is the strategy for launching a product to the world: who it is for, how it will be positioned, and how it will reach people. It ties product, marketing, and sales into one launch approach.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: A strong product can still flop with a weak launch. This plan gives the release the best shot at landing with its audience.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Built in Discovery and refined toward launch, it pulls together positioning, personas, pricing, and the release and marketing plans.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Deliverable Description: A project hand-off is the package of work, notes, and context passed on when a project or phase ends. It makes sure the next team or the client can pick things up cleanly.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: Good hand-offs prevent knowledge from walking out the door, so momentum and understanding are not lost at the finish line.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Delivered around Launch, it gathers up the artifacts made across the whole project into one clear, usable summary.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

Project Milestones: Intake
Deliverable Description: A statement of work is the agreement that spells out what a project will deliver, on what timeline, and under what terms. It sets the shared expectations at the very start.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It prevents misunderstandings later by getting everyone to agree, in writing, on what success looks like before the work begins.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Created during Intake, it anchors the project plan, goals, and KPIs, and it is the reference point the team returns to when scope questions arise.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

Project Milestones: MVP Design Requirements, MMP Design Requirements, MMP Development Requirements, MVP Development Requirements
Deliverable Description: Prioritized backlog tasks are the to-do items for a product, sorted so the most valuable work sits on top. The backlog is the team's ordered pile of everything worth doing.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: A clear order means the team always knows what to pull next, so effort goes to what matters most instead of what is nearest.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Shaped in Requirements from user stories and priorities, the backlog feeds sprint planning and gets re-ordered constantly as things change.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Deliverable Description: A how-might-we statement reframes a problem as an open question that invites solutions, like 'how might we make sign-up feel effortless?' It turns a pain point into a springboard for ideas.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: Framing problems this way opens up creative thinking instead of locking the team into the first fix that comes to mind.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: They come out of Discovery from problem statements and research, and they kick off ideation that leads toward scope and design.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Set during Intake alongside goals and OKRs, they guide decisions across the whole project and show up again in analytics and testing.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

Project Milestones: MVP Release Vision, MMP Release Vision
Deliverable Description: OKRs pair a clear objective with a few measurable results that show you are getting there. They connect a big goal to concrete signs of progress.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: They keep a team aligned on what matters and make it obvious whether the work is moving the needle or just staying busy.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Defined in Intake next to KPIs and project goals, they frame priorities that ripple into the roadmap and backlog.

Deliverable Description: A Gantt chart is a timeline view of a project's tasks, showing what happens when and what overlaps. It gives a bird's-eye view of the schedule.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It helps a team see how work fits together over time and spot crunches early, though in agile work it stays a living guide, not a fixed promise.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Created around Intake, it works with the project plan and roadmap and gets updated as milestones progress and plans shift.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

Project Milestones: MVP Design, MVP Development, MMP Development

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Used across all milestones during sprints, it draws on the sprint plan and goals and feeds retrospective conversations.

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Shaped in the Vision milestone, it sits above scope, epics, and the release plan and gets revisited as priorities evolve.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

Project Milestones: Intake

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Made from the refined backlog and sprint goals, it drives the burn down chart and the demo and retro that close the sprint.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

Deliverable Description: Wireframes are simple, low-detail sketches of a screen's layout, showing where things go without color or polish. They focus on structure, not looks.

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Created in the Implement milestone from task flows and requirements, they are the first step toward low- and high-fidelity prototypes.

Deliverable Description: A low-fidelity prototype is a rough, clickable version of a product used to test ideas quickly. It is more interactive than a wireframe but far from finished.

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Built in Implement from wireframes, it feeds usability testing and grows into high-fidelity prototypes as ideas hold up.
Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: It builds on low-fidelity prototypes in Implement and hands developers a clear target, backed by UI specs and the design system.

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Created in Implement from high-fidelity prototypes, they pair with design annotations and the design system to guide developers.

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Produced in Requirements or Implement from heuristics analysis and analytics, it points toward design changes and research follow-ups.

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Made in Discovery from research, it works alongside personas and journey maps to shape design decisions.
Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

Deliverable Description: A storyboard tells the story of how someone experiences a product through a series of simple frames, like a comic strip. It shows the experience in context, moment by moment.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: It helps a team imagine the real-world situation around a product, not just the screens, which sparks more human design ideas.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Created in Discovery, it builds on journey maps and personas and feeds early design and ideation work.
Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

Deliverable Description: Sketches are quick, hand-drawn ideas for a design, made fast and cheap to explore lots of directions. They are thinking on paper.

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Done in Implement during rapid ideation, they are the loose starting point that firms up into wireframes and prototypes.
Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

Deliverable Description: A task analysis breaks down exactly how a user accomplishes a task, step by step. It examines the how of a task in fine detail.
Why Is This Deliverable Important?: Understanding each step reveals where users struggle, so the team can simplify the hardest parts.
How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Created in Discovery from research planning, it informs task flows, journey maps, and the designs that follow.
Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

Deliverable Description: A research report gathers what a study found and what it means into one clear document. It turns raw research into shareable insight.

How Does This Deliverable Relate to Othe: Produced in Discovery from many research activities, it feeds personas, journey maps, and the priorities the team sets next.
